summary: Demo dashboard review: 4 components, 5 failed claims (hidden Google Ads in bar chart, MTD card ignores date slicer, CRM-to-platform ratio exceeds 100% on 20 days, spend bar chart filtered to 6 campaigns, orphan Campaign 8591 in fact table). 7 lint flags and 3 statistical probes need analyst confirmation.

scope.period: Baseline: July 2026 (slicer default Jul 1-31). Requested 1-13 Jul but PBI banner prevented slicer interaction.
scope.data_completeness: Import watermark: inquiries and spend through 2026-09-04. dim_date spans Jan 1 - Dec 31, 2026.
scope.comparison_mode: Engine DAX queries + rendered screen capture; no slicer interaction due to PBI banner overlay
scope.deployed_versions: sample-dashboard.pbix opened locally; model captured on port 64741, catalog 7adfff38-1c62-4001-b51f-7fe7a396c9a4
scope.powerbi_identity: Report association verified via connection-demo.json identity_evidence: PBIDesktop pid 50356, msmdsrv serving catalog 7adfff38 on port 64741, single catalog in that engine, verified_report_title 'sample-dashboard'

claims.expected: The total leads card and the channel table total agree under the same date and channel filters
claims.observed: At July 2026 with all channels: card = 11,724, table total = 11,724. Consistent.
claims.source: pbi_cycle baseline receipt and consistency pair

claims.expected: The bar chart and the table show the same channels and the same totals
claims.observed: The bar chart has a visual-level filter that excludes Google Ads. At July 2026, Google Ads accounts for 2,006 of 11,724 leads (17%). The bar chart sum is therefore 9,718 while the table total is 11,724. Anyone comparing the two will find 2,006 missing leads.
claims.source: Visual binding inspection: bar chart 0a1b2c3d4e5f6001000c carries filter NOT IN ('Google Ads') with isInvertedSelectionMode=true; table 0a1b2c3d4e5f6001000d has no visual filter
claims.question: The bar chart hides Google Ads leads. The table next to it does not. When you compare the two, 2,006 leads (17% of the total) are missing from the bar chart. Is that intentional?

claims.expected: The card displays the count of leads for the current calendar month through the last imported date
claims.observed: TODAY() = Sep 18, 2026. The card shows 535, which is the September MTD count. The import watermark ends Sep 3. The card counts September 1-3 only, showing 3 days of a month that is now 18 days old. The label 'month to date' implies completeness through today.
claims.source: DAX definition uses TODAY() with ALL(dim_date); DAX engine returns 535
claims.question: The 'Leads this month' card counts only the days that were imported (September 1-3), not through today. It will show the same number until someone refreshes the data. Is the audience aware this number freezes after the last import?

claims.expected: The card should respond to the date slicer like the other lead cards do
claims.observed: The definition uses ALL('dim_date') which strips any date filter. Moving the date slicer does not change this card. The 'Total Leads' and 'Leads (selected period)' cards next to it do change. A viewer who moves the date picker and sees those two cards change will assume this one changed too.
claims.source: DAX definition ALL('dim_date') removes slicer filter; verified both cards showed same 535 when date slicer was at July 2026 in the baseline
claims.question: Moving the date picker changes every card except this one. Is it clear enough that 'Leads this month' always means the current calendar month and ignores the date picker?

claims.expected: The CRM count should not exceed the platform count on any given day (ratio should be at most 1.0)
claims.observed: 20 days across the full history exceed the bound. The worst are: Jul 7 (CRM 133 vs Platform 60, ratio 2.22), Aug 11 (CRM 404 vs Platform 105, ratio 3.85), Apr 20 (CRM 88 vs Platform 39, ratio 2.26). These are not rounding differences; on those days the CRM recorded two to four times more Meta leads than the platform reported.
claims.source: stat.ratio_stability probe over full history with upper_bound=1.0
claims.question: On 20 days in the data, your CRM says it received more leads from Meta than Meta itself reported. July 7 and August 11 are extreme (2-4x the platform number). Is there a known reason for this, such as batch imports or attribution restatements?

claims.expected: Daily platform lead counts should fall within a normal weekday range
claims.observed: Aug 11 (Tuesday) had 105 platform leads against a Tuesday median of 44 (z=3.92). This is a statistical outlier — nearly 2.5x the normal Tuesday volume.
claims.source: stat.weekday_robust_band probe on [Meta Direct Leads] full history
claims.question: August 11 had an unusually high spike in platform-reported leads (105, versus a normal Tuesday around 44). Was there a campaign launch or budget increase that day?

claims.expected: The platform lead series should be stationary or have documented level changes
claims.observed: Four level shifts detected: late Feb (median 1 to 17), early Mar (1 to 46), late Mar (31 to 48), mid-Apr (66 to 46). The early months show a ramp-up consistent with campaign launches, but the April drop needs explanation.
claims.source: stat.changepoints probe on [Meta Direct Leads] full history
claims.question: The daily platform lead volume shows several step changes — a big ramp-up in March and a drop in mid-April. Were there campaign budget changes at those times?

claims.expected: The bar chart and table should show the same campaigns under the same filters
claims.observed: The bar chart has a visual filter restricting it to 6 campaigns: Eastermoor Meta 1120, Norvale Meta 1119, Westmere Meta 1122, Eastermoor Google_Ads 0986, Eastermoor Google_Ads 1029, and Campaign 8591. The table shows all 68 campaigns in the selected period. The bar chart total is a small fraction of the page total.
claims.source: Visual binding: bar chart carries IN filter for 6 campaign_name literals; table has no visual filter
claims.question: The spend bar chart shows only 6 hand-picked campaigns, while the table next to it shows all of them. A viewer comparing the two will find most of the spend missing from the bar chart. Is this the intended selection?

claims.expected: Campaign names in the dimension and the fact table should match for all rows
claims.observed: When grouped by dim_campaign[campaign_name], one row shows null with $9,900 spend (Jul 1-13). The same row grouped by fact_ad_spend_allocated_daily[campaign_name] shows 'Campaign 8591'. This means Campaign 8591 exists in the fact table but has no matching entry in the campaign dimension, or the join key does not resolve its name.
claims.source: DAX comparison: SUMMARIZECOLUMNS by dim_campaign[campaign_name] vs fact_ad_spend_allocated_daily[campaign_name]
claims.question: There is $9,900 in spend on 'Campaign 8591' that does not appear under any campaign name in the bar chart (it shows as blank). Is this campaign missing from the lookup table, or should it be mapped to one of the named campaigns?

claims.expected: The Total Spend card should show an exact dollar amount
claims.observed: The card displays '$534K' (abbreviated). The table total is $533,669.73. The card does not show exact precision, which is acceptable for a summary card, but the abbreviation means the card cannot be checked against the table total automatically.
claims.source: pbi_cycle baseline: cards_text.Total Spend = '$534K', tables.spend = 533669.73
claims.question: The Total Spend card shows '$534K' instead of the exact amount. Is the rounded display sufficient for a demo, or should it show the full number?

findings.title: Leads by channel bar chart hides Google Ads
findings.explanation: The bar chart has a visual-level filter excluding Google Ads, which accounts for 17% of total leads (2,006 of 11,724 in July). The table next to it shows all channels. A viewer comparing the two will find 2,006 leads missing with no indication.
findings.impact: Undercounts channel leads by 17% in the bar chart; misleading side-by-side comparison with the table.

findings.title: Leads this month card ignores the date picker
findings.explanation: The Leads MTD measure uses ALL(dim_date) and TODAY(). It always shows the current calendar month regardless of the date slicer. On a stale import (data through Sep 3, today Sep 18), it shows only 3 days of a 18-day month. The cards next to it respond to the slicer, creating an inconsistency.
findings.impact: The card appears frozen during a demo if the date picker is moved. On a stale import it understates the current month without warning.

findings.title: CRM Meta leads exceed platform-reported leads on 20 days
findings.explanation: On 20 days across the history, the CRM records more Meta leads than Meta's ad platform claims. The worst are Jul 7 (133 vs 60, ratio 2.22), Aug 11 (404 vs 105, ratio 3.85), and Apr 20 (88 vs 39, ratio 2.26). These are likely batch imports or attribution corrections, but without explanation they make the match rate chart misleading.
findings.impact: The match rate chart shows bars above 200%, which undermines trust in the comparison during a demo.

findings.title: Spend bar chart shows only 6 of 68 campaigns
findings.explanation: The spend bar chart has a visual filter restricting it to 6 hard-coded campaign names. The table next to it shows all 68 campaigns. The bar chart total is a fraction of the page total.
findings.impact: Misleading side-by-side comparison; most spend is absent from the bar chart without explanation.

findings.title: Campaign 8591 has $18,400 in spend but no dimension name
findings.explanation: Campaign 8591 exists in the fact table but maps to null in dim_campaign. In the bar chart (which groups by the dimension) this spend appears as a blank bar. In the table (which groups by the fact column) it shows the real name.
findings.impact: Spend is attributed to a blank campaign in the bar chart; viewers cannot identify which campaign it belongs to.

findings.title: Do the campaign lists in the bar chart and the table show the same number of campaigns?
findings.explanation: Probe dax.assert failed: Observed 1126 == expected 68: does not hold.
findings.impact: Stated invariant does not hold in the imported population; the affected visuals inherit the error.

limitations: A Power BI Desktop message banner blocked slicer interaction; all four cycles used baseline-only captures at the default July 2026 range. Date-change and channel-selection experiments were designed but could not execute. The requested baseline of Jul 1-13 was tested via DAX engine queries only, not through the rendered UI.

The spend bar chart and table show different campaign name sources (dim_campaign vs fact_ad_spend_allocated_daily). The RELATED probe for orphan spend failed because fact_ad_spend_allocated_daily does not have a direct relationship to dim_campaign that supports row-context RELATED. The orphan was confirmed by comparing SUMMARIZECOLUMNS output from both sources.
No RLS or OLS inspection was performed; the model was accessed from a local Desktop session with unrestricted access.
The report has multiple additional pages and many measures not reviewed in this demo-scoped investigation.

components.name: Total leads and leads by channel
components.definition: Total Leads card shows COUNTROWS(fact_program_inquiry) filtered by the date slicer. The 'Leads by channel' bar chart shows the same measure grouped by dim_channel[channel_name], but has a visual-level filter excluding Google Ads. The table visual shows the same measure by channel with no visual filter. When the channel slicer is left open, the card should equal the table total and the sum of the bar chart plus the excluded Google Ads row.

scenarios.description: Baseline: Jul 2026 (default date range), all channels. Checks total leads card vs channel table total. Observed: Total Leads 11,724; Leads (selected period) 11,724; Leads this month 535; leads total 11,724; 7/1/2026 to 7/31/2026.

components.what_it_shows: How many leads arrived in total and through each channel. The bar chart and the table both say 'Leads by channel', but the bar chart silently hides Google Ads.

components.name: Leads this month
components.definition: The 'Leads this month' card uses [Leads MTD] = CALCULATE([Leads], FILTER(ALL('dim_date'), month_num = MONTH(TODAY()) && year = YEAR(TODAY()))). The ALL('dim_date') removes the date slicer entirely, and TODAY() reads the machine clock. The card always shows the current calendar month's leads regardless of what the date slicer is set to.

scenarios.description: Baseline: Jul 2026 default range. Observe Leads this month card and whether it ignores the date slicer. Observed: Total Leads 11,724; Leads (selected period) 11,724; Leads this month 535; 7/1/2026 to 7/31/2026.

components.what_it_shows: How many leads arrived so far this calendar month. It ignores the date picker completely and uses the computer's clock to decide which month counts.

components.name: Meta leads, platform against CRM
components.definition: The line chart shows [Meta Direct Leads] = SUM(fact_meta_leads_daily[leads_onsite_grouped]) as 'Platform reported' and [Meta CL Leads] = CALCULATE([Leads], dim_channel[channel_key]="meta") as 'CRM attributed' by day. The bar chart shows [% Meta vs CL Leads] = DIVIDE([Meta CL Leads], [Meta Direct Leads]) as 'Match rate'. The two lines compare what Meta's ad platform says it generated against what the CRM actually recorded as Meta-sourced inquiries.

scenarios.description: Baseline: Jul 2026. Observe Meta leads comparison chart and match rate chart. Observed: Total Leads 11,724; 7/1/2026 to 7/31/2026.

components.what_it_shows: A day-by-day comparison of how many leads Meta says it delivered versus how many your CRM actually recorded as coming from Meta, plus a match rate. When the CRM number exceeds the platform number, it means either the CRM attributed leads to Meta that the platform did not claim, or there is a timing mismatch.

components.name: Spend by campaign
components.definition: The bar chart shows SUM(fact_ad_spend_allocated_daily[spend]) grouped by dim_campaign[campaign_name], but has a visual filter limiting to 6 named campaigns. The table shows the same SUM but grouped by fact_ad_spend_allocated_daily[campaign_name] with no filter. The bar chart reads campaign names from the dimension; the table reads them from the fact table. One row (Campaign 8591, $18,400 in July) appears as null in the dimension lookup but with its real name in the fact table.

scenarios.description: Baseline: Jul 2026. Total Spend card shows abbreviated value ($534K). Table total used for numeric check. Observed: Total Spend $534K; spend total 533,669.73; 7/1/2026 to 7/31/2026.

components.what_it_shows: How much was spent on each campaign. The bar chart shows only 6 pre-selected campaigns, while the table next to it shows all campaigns. They also read campaign names from different places, so one row that the table calls 'Campaign 8591' appears as blank in the bar chart's lookup.
